Retained as high-value watch because the primary contribution is model architecture/training rather than a standalone serving/runtime mechanism.

historical_watchlist.title: Diffusion Language Models for Mobile Edge Agentic AI: Foundations, Applications, and Challenges
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / diffusion language models / edge-cloud serving / mobile edge AI
historical_watchlist.why: 30d edge/agent replay recovered a systems-oriented survey absent from the authority union. It connects DLM parallel refinement and quality-latency elasticity to edge constraints including memory, energy, bandwidth, split inference, communication-aware serving, long-context state, and multimodal grounding. High lineage value, but its primary contribution is survey/taxonomy rather than a new runtime mechanism, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Drift-Aware LLM Routing with Sparse Contexts and Shared Budgets
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / multi-model routing / nonstationary workloads / resource budgets
historical_watchlist.why: 30d edge/heterogeneous replay recovered a relevant multi-model routing formulation absent from authority. DRS handles high-dimensional sparse prompt contexts, workload/model-frontier drift, multiple compute/latency/memory/cost budgets, online shadow prices, and hard admission meters. The contribution is currently theory-heavy with limited production-runtime evidence, so retain as high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond Semantic Organization: Memory as Execution State Management for Long-Horizon Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-horizon memory / context compression
historical_watchlist.why: Execution-state-tree agent memory with explicit Grow/Compress/Maintain/Revise operations; primary paper reports 7.8-20.4 pp task-success gain and 55.1% lower token consumption. High-value systems-adjacent agent-memory mechanism, retained as watch pending stronger runtime/deployment evidence.

historical_watchlist.title: RACE-AIMC: Selective Inference for Heterogeneous Analog In-Memory Accelerators at the Edge
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / analog in-memory accelerator / selective inference
historical_watchlist.why: Relevant heterogeneous edge-AI accelerator routing framework with certified selective inference and modeled 69.02% energy reduction versus always running all accelerators, but current evidence is simulation-only and lacks a strong systems venue, so retain as high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Same Request, Different Answer: Quantization Amplifies Cache-Induced Divergence in LLM Serving
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / prefix cache / quantization / reproducibility
historical_watchlist.why: Direct serving-path measurement showing prefix-cache state can materially change multi-turn agent trajectories, with divergence increasing from 36.2% at 16-bit to 75.0% at 4-bit across two engines. Important cache+quantization systems reliability signal, but it is primarily a measurement/reproducibility study and currently only submitted to IEEE Access, so keep as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Reasoning Without Inference Cost: Latent Semantic Scaffolding for Robot VLA Policies
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / zero-overhead reasoning / deployment efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI signal. Training-only semantic scaffolding aligns action-token representations to physical-reasoning rationale embeddings and drops the projection head at deployment, leaving the base VLA with zero added inference cost. Strong deployment-efficiency idea but primarily algorithmic and currently preprint-only, so high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Continual Field-Adaptive Models (CFAMs) for Post-Deployment Physical AI
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / on-device adaptation / post-deployment runtime
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI deployment signal. CFAM performs autonomous gradient-free on-device post-deployment updates across five embodiments and reports 2.5x fewer prior-training trajectories plus +13.9pp action success after near-OOD field updates. Systems/deployment relevance is real, but the contribution remains model/learning-framework heavy and lacks a strong systems venue, so high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: FAVE: Foveated Adaptive Visual Encoding for Efficient Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / visual-token efficiency / adaptive encoding
historical_watchlist.why: Strong MLLM efficiency signal: variable-resolution foveated encoding, 12.7x lower FLOPs in a controlled small-object setting and 3.3x controlled TTFT speedup when integrated with FastVLM. Current contribution is primarily model/encoding design rather than a full serving-system paper, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Sustainable Edge Vision via Empirically Calibrated DVFS: Eliminating Thermal Throttling on Passively Cooled Hardware
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / DVFS / thermal-aware inference
historical_watchlist.why: Real hardware edge-inference scheduler on passively cooled Raspberry Pi 5. Eliminates observed thermal throttling, improves frame rate by 6.8% versus temperature-only control and reduces energy/frame by 1.9%; scope is narrow, so high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Deep Microcompression: Structured Pruning and Bit-packed Quantization for Microcontrollers
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / microcontroller inference / pruning / quantization
historical_watchlist.why: Hardware-aware MCU deployment pipeline combining structured pruning, QAT and fixed-length bit-packing; reports 55.8x weight compression and deployment on ATmega328P with 2KB SRAM. Valuable edge-AI systems signal but currently limited-model/MCU scope.

historical_watchlist.title: APEX-RBD: Mixed-Precision Exploration Framework for Hardware-Efficient Robot Dynamics Accelerator Design
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot accelerator / mixed precision / edge hardware
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-efficiency candidate. Automates mixed-precision design-space exploration for rigid-body-dynamics accelerators and reports up to 1.9x area reduction and 1.8x power savings across robotic platforms; valuable but focused on dynamics hardware rather than learned policy serving.

historical_watchlist.title: GeoSPRINT: Geometric Redundancy-Aware Step Pruning for Inference in Diffusion Trajectories
historical_watchlist.why: Training-free diffusion acceleration via geometric redundancy-aware nonuniform sampling schedules. Improves FID over uniform DDIM at matched NFE budgets across CIFAR-10, LSUN Church and Stable Diffusion v1.5; promising algorithmic acceleration but no direct wall-clock/runtime systems evidence yet.

historical_watchlist.title: Training-Free Halving of Activated Experts in Fine-Grained Mixture-of-Experts Models
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / expert pruning / inference efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: Training-free method separates active expert count from probability-mass normalization, halving routed-expert compute on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with only 0.35 MMLU-point loss and replicating on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. Strong algorithmic MoE-efficiency signal but lacks measured serving latency/throughput.

historical_watchlist.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
historical_watchlist.why: Training- and calibration-free token-adaptive expert skipping with offline spectral/prototype statistics and lightweight runtime table lookups. Strong quality at 50% expert skipping across multiple MoE LLMs, but current abstract lacks measured end-to-end systems speedup.

historical_watchlist.title: JLIR: A Julia-Native MLIR-Inspired Intermediate Representation with Automatic JACC Kernel Extraction
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / Julia IR / accelerator kernel extraction
historical_watchlist.why: Compiler-infrastructure contribution bringing MLIR-style extensible IR into Julia with automatic JACC accelerator-kernel extraction. Relevant to DSL/compiler route, but current primary evidence does not yet establish strong AI-workload performance impact.

historical_watchlist.title: SCX Router: Streaming Zero-Shot Model Selection with a Decoder-KV Classifier and a Real-World Task Ontology
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / KV-cache reuse
historical_watchlist.why: Lightweight 0.6B zero-shot inference router preserves decoder KV across sessions and evaluates transient candidate labels without polluting persistent cache; directly relevant to serving model selection, but current primary evidence emphasizes routing quality rather than end-to-end latency/cost measurements.

historical_watchlist.title: Importance-Aware Low-Rank Distillation of Diffusion Transformers
historical_watchlist.why: SVDtrunc allocates low-rank compression across DiT blocks and retains near-full FLUX.dev quality at 68% of original parameter count while remaining competitive at 57%; strong deployment-efficiency signal but no direct measured latency/throughput result in the primary abstract.

historical_watchlist.title: Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / cloud-edge robotics / communication-aware world models
historical_watchlist.why: Couples control and wireless JEPA world models to predict robot and channel state and schedule uplink transmissions, explicitly targeting communication-efficient remote robotic control; currently validated in Gazebo-ROS-Sionna simulation rather than production deployment.

historical_watchlist.title: Compact-Memory LLM Agents via Online Max-Member Clustering and Atom-Aware Packing
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory compression / long-horizon agents
historical_watchlist.why: Online clustered memory reaches 83% of full-context quality at 32% of token cost under a 4k budget and improves over streaming-cluster baselines; relevant to efficient long-horizon agents, though current evidence is token-budget efficiency rather than serving-system latency.

historical_watchlist.title: Fast Gauss Sums via Flash Attention
historical_watchlist.why: Maps arbitrary signed Gaussian kernel sums onto FlashAttention using small input augmentations, outperforming compiled PyTorch and PyKeOps for D>8 in fp16 while keeping linear memory scaling; useful kernel-reuse result, but it targets kernel methods rather than mainstream AI-inference workloads.

historical_watchlist.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
historical_watchlist.why: Extends SparseGPT with a bias-aware second-order term and evaluates 25%, 50%, and 2:4 structured sparsity while preserving perplexity and zero-shot accuracy. Relevant pruning follow-up, but the primary contribution is fairness-quality rather than measured runtime/system acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: GPU-Accelerated Astrodynamics World Models for Spacecraft Rendezvous and Proximity Operations
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / GPU simulation
historical_watchlist.why: Introduces an open-source JAX GPU-parallel spacecraft environment and a flow-matching world model for autonomous rendezvous, with improved sample efficiency and docking success. It is a useful Physical-AI world-model/runtime signal, but not yet a serving or deployment-efficiency paper.

historical_watchlist.title: TAP-Path: Task-Adaptive Structural and Token Pruning for Efficient and Trustworthy Pathology Foundation Models
historical_watchlist.why: Combines transformer-block removal and adaptive patch-token pruning, reducing encoder parameters by about 25% and analytical compute by 35.2% while preserving or improving pathology accuracy. Strong compression signal but currently domain-specific and without measured systems latency.

historical_watchlist.title: ProtLingo: Efficient Protein Language Modeling via Conditional Memory and Expert Routing
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / conditional memory / efficient language models
historical_watchlist.why: Combines conditional local memory with sparse expert routing in a protein language model and activates only a subset of expert parameters. Interesting efficiency mechanism, but primary evidence focuses on parameter/task efficiency rather than end-to-end systems latency or throughput.

historical_watchlist.title: Who Speaks for the Pruned? Visual Token Pruning as Coverage Optimization
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / sparsity/pruning / visual token pruning
historical_watchlist.why: CoverPruner formulates training-free visual-token pruning as representational coverage maximization and reports the best average accuracy across multiple VLMs and compression rates, especially under aggressive pruning. It directly targets inference cost, but the current abstract does not provide end-to-end latency or throughput measurements.

historical_watchlist.title: SCULPT: Training Edge Vision Models for Post-Training Quantization Readiness
historical_watchlist.why: SCULPT shapes activation distributions during ordinary FP32 training so models are easier to post-train quantize, exporting learned clipping bounds to standard INT8/W4A8 deployment without runtime transforms. It reports a large W8A8 accuracy recovery on EfficientNet-B0, but has limited systems-scale latency evidence.

historical_watchlist.title: XMerge: Cross-Axis Selection and Reconstructive Layer Merging for LLM Depth Compression
historical_watchlist.why: XMerge removes complete transformer layers while preserving the standard serving architecture and reconstructs local boundaries to reduce quality loss. It reports decode savings sufficient to amortize construction cost after tens of thousands of requests, but lacks a strong end-to-end production serving benchmark.

historical_watchlist.title: Post-Training Ternarization of Qwen3-4B Capability, Effective Bit Budget, Storage Compression, and Deployment
historical_watchlist.why: This study converts Qwen3-4B to 1.641 effective bits per quantized linear weight and packs the model from 8.29 GiB to 3.96 GiB, explicitly auditing deployment behavior. It is valuable as a negative systems result because its preliminary Triton GEMV is 4.6x slower than FP16 cuBLAS, showing storage compression does not automatically yield inference speedup.

historical_watchlist.title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back in Low-Precision Temporal Inference
historical_watchlist.why: Shows that deterministic 4-bit recurrent-state storage can catastrophically amplify error over time, and that error-feedback/residual-memory write-back can recover accuracy without retraining. The result is domain-specific but exposes a general systems interface issue for low-precision stateful inference.

historical_watchlist.title: Selective Agent Guidance via Entropy: Learning Autonomous Policies from Imperfect VLM Teachers
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / distillation
historical_watchlist.why: SAGE queries an expensive VLM teacher only on uncertain training steps and distills useful guidance into a lightweight autonomous policy; deployment requires no VLM calls. This is a strong efficiency signal for embodied/interactive agents, but current evidence emphasizes learning quality and teacher-query reduction rather than serving latency.

historical_watchlist.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multimodal reasoning / CoT compression / KV pressure
historical_watchlist.why: Strong efficiency signal for multimodal reasoning: fewer than 900 training samples, up to 69.5% CoT-length reduction and up to 3.34x end-to-end inference speedup while preserving accuracy. Contribution is primarily algorithmic preference/compression rather than a serving-system design, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: LookStep: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation with Linguistic Foresight and Event Driven Memory
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embodied navigation / bounded memory
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI efficiency signal. Replaces accumulated frames/cognitive maps with event-driven bounded rolling memory and linguistic future-state modeling; reports 49.7% R2R-CE Val-Unseen success with better memory efficiency and less data, with official author code/model release. Current paper emphasizes policy/task quality more than measured end-to-end serving latency, so keep as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Network-Aware Forecasting on Wireless Access Points
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / on-device inference / resource contention
historical_watchlist.why: Useful real deployment measurement for inference sharing an enterprise AP with packet processing. Five implementations run 6.1-19.1x slower on target AP than Raspberry Pi 5; two similarly sized foundation models differ 19x in AP latency; 13-stream serving under network saturation raises p99 RTT 76% and cuts throughput 7.06%. Primarily a measurement/deployability study rather than a new runtime, so watchlist-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Compute-in-Memory Attention: A Time-Domain Analog Softmax Circuit with RC-Tunable Temperature
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / AI accelerator / compute-in-memory / analog softmax
historical_watchlist.why: Relevant attention-accelerator circuit that eliminates an intermediate ADC path by applying tunable time-domain analog softmax directly to CIM score voltages. Post-layout 22-nm simulations report 242.97 ns, 13.44 mW and 25.5 pJ/output element for 128-way softmax, with hardware-aware Transformer loss within 2.5% of ideal. Simulation-only evidence keeps it watchlist-high rather than canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Lngram v2: Latent N-Gram Memory with Interpretable Discrete Representations
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / multimodal serving / conditional memory / efficient model architecture
historical_watchlist.why: Promising efficient memory mechanism that decouples route count, memory dimension and backbone width, with grouped-query readout and hard discrete addressing. Scales to a 30B VLM while substantially reducing total and activated memory parameters, but current evidence emphasizes model/parameter efficiency rather than measured serving latency or throughput.

historical_watchlist.title: Flip, Don't Shuffle: Watermarking LLMs at the Speed of Inference
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / inference kernel / watermarking overhead
historical_watchlist.why: Stateless Bernoulli Watermarking reduces token membership to O(1), supports single-kernel execution with zero intermediate allocations and distributed inference, and reports <1% end-to-end generation overhead. Accepted at EMNLP 2026 Main, but watermarking is adjacent rather than a core serving primitive, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Scalable Kronecker-Fisher Approximation: Efficient Hessian Analysis for Billion-Parameter Language Models Compression
historical_watchlist.why: Scalable Kronecker-based Fisher/Hessian approximation captures cross-layer sensitivity for billion-parameter models without materializing the full matrix and correlates with degradation/recovery under quantization and sparsification. Useful for mixed-precision and sparsity allocation, but current contribution is analysis/methodology rather than demonstrated end-to-end serving acceleration.

historical_watchlist.title: Modeling What Changes: Sparse, Residual World Models for Object-Centric Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / sparse world models / object-centric prediction
historical_watchlist.why: Sparse change-gated residual world model predicts only changing objects, giving 8.6-11.1x fewer parameters and 2.5-4.6x better next-state pose accuracy than a dense baseline on 3-8 object MuJoCo pushing, with lower rollout drift and cross-object-count transfer. Strong Physical-AI efficiency signal, but planning success remains early and no deployment/runtime latency is shown, so retain as protected high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Proton Irradiation Characterization of an Open-Source ML Accelerator on a Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / Physical AI / FPGA accelerator reliability
historical_watchlist.why: System-level proton-irradiation study of an open-source Tensil neural-network accelerator on Zynq UltraScale+ running ResNet-20 inference, documenting availability loss and silent output corruption with implications for recovery and verifiable edge/space AI deployment. Important Physical-AI/edge accelerator reliability evidence, but not primarily an efficiency or acceleration contribution.

historical_watchlist.title: HINT: Human-Intent Inception for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / sparse semantic reasoning / low-latency control
historical_watchlist.why: Invokes semantic reasoning only at manipulation-pattern transitions, then uses continuous multi-view grounding/tracking, with no added trainable parameters in the foundation action model and reported low-latency control across two policies. Strong protected Physical-AI efficiency signal, but the paper does not yet provide sufficiently detailed systems latency/throughput evidence for canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: RVSD: Retrieval Vision Sparse Decoding for Mitigating Visual Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / sparse decoding / visual token retrieval
historical_watchlist.why: Training-free single-pass LVLM decoding combines semantics-directed visual-token sparsification with on-demand semantic-space visual retrieval, explicitly avoiding multi-round decoding overhead while retaining long-context hallucination suppression. Relevant inference design, but current public evidence is quality-centric and lacks hard end-to-end latency/throughput gains.

historical_watchlist.title: LookThere! Sparse Vision by Reinforced Selection
historical_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / adaptive vision inference / edge-efficient perception
historical_watchlist.why: End-to-end learned selector/extractor achieves a new performance-compute Pareto frontier and can retain accuracy with as little as 0.2% of the input on sparse high-resolution tasks, generalizing across classification, segmentation and regression. Strong adaptive-compute signal, but primarily a vision algorithm rather than AI-infra/serving system, so keep as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: One MLLM, One Call: Efficient Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation via Spatial-Aware Waypoints
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / VLN / sparse MLLM invocation / robot navigation
historical_watchlist.why: O2C-Nav reduces zero-shot VLN-CE to a single MLLM call per decision step using structured waypoints, explicit spatial markers, and a low-level FMM planner, directly targeting inference latency and visual-processing overhead. It outperforms prior zero-shot methods and releases code, but the current primary abstract does not provide hard end-to-end latency/throughput numbers, so retain as protected high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive layer routing / cached VLM representations
historical_watchlist.why: LayerRoute dynamically mixes cached VLM-layer representations and rereads prior action states for VLA control, improving StarVLA-pi and pi0.5 across simulation and real-world benchmarks with only 0.31%/3.87% added parameters. It is highly relevant to adaptive representation access and cache reuse, but the current evidence emphasizes task quality rather than measured inference speedup, so retain as protected high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: MetaKV: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Constrained LLM Inference
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / adaptive compression / constrained inference
historical_watchlist.why: MetaKV predicts latency, peak memory, and correctness for multiple KV compression configurations and selects per-prompt settings under user budgets. Across KVQuant, H2O, RocketKV and FP16 it improves constrained success rate by about 0.07 on average and up to 0.135 over the best static configuration; useful systems direction, but the primary result is budget satisfaction rather than a direct end-to-end speedup, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Unified AI Gateway: A Framework for Joint Model Routing and KV Cache Management
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / KV cache management / edge-cloud placement
historical_watchlist.why: Unified AI Gateway jointly reasons about model choice, execution site, and KV-cache actions under quality, latency, cost and resource constraints, with analytical workload simulations reporting 1.25-13.28x TTFT and 1.20-6.16x input-cost benefits. It is strategically relevant but is primarily a synthesis/framework with simulation rather than a new measured deployed system, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: RouteRelay: Event-Triggered Cross-Layer Route Reuse for Efficient Dynamic Sparse Attention
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / sparse attention / route reuse / GPU kernels
historical_watchlist.why: RouteRelay reuses sparse-attention routing metadata across layers and selectively reroutes rows only when sentinel chunks challenge the retained route. It reaches at least 99.99% route recall and evaluates 38.4-51.6% of full-routing score pairs at larger routing scales, but its current unfused CPU implementation remains slower than dense matrix multiplication, so this is an important systems watch rather than canonical-high yet.

historical_watchlist.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / LLM inference / measurement
historical_watchlist.why: This controlled study measures accuracy, footprint, prefill latency, per-token latency and execution energy across Jetson AGX Orin and near-edge CPU/GPU nodes, including quantized open models and cloud GPT-4o as a reference. It provides useful placement and Pareto evidence but introduces no new serving mechanism, so retain as a high-value measurement watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning
historical_watchlist.why: OverRep temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training and algebraically merges it into an inference-time compact module. It improves retained reasoning by up to 5.5 and 8.4 points at 25% and 50% structured pruning while preserving the compact deployed architecture, but current evidence emphasizes quality recovery rather than measured latency, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation
historical_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / dense vision / single-step inference
historical_watchlist.why: Marigold V2 converts pretrained multi-step flow-matching image models into single-step dense-regression inference, with quantization where needed, while improving KITTI/ETH3D AbsRel by 16-26% over the previous best. The step-count reduction is strategically relevant to diffusion/flow acceleration, but the current abstract does not report measured end-to-end latency or throughput, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for On-Device Fire Understanding
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge inference / VLM distillation
historical_watchlist.why: This work distills domain-specialized VLMs into compact students and deploys them on a commercial Detectium fire sensor, jointly measuring reasoning accuracy, latency and memory. It is valuable real-device MLLM deployment evidence, but the abstract does not report a concrete speedup or latency reduction, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: RAGMark: A Comprehensive Framework for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
historical_watchlist.why: RAGMark is a modular multi-GPU RAG benchmark collecting per-stage latency, TTFT, throughput, GPU utilization, memory, power and quality. Its experiments expose cross-stage bottleneck shifts and show reranking plus compression can lower energy by up to 66%, but the contribution is primarily measurement infrastructure rather than a new serving mechanism.

historical_watchlist.title: MoEMB: Scaling Universal Multimodal Embeddings with Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Models
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / MoE systems / retrieval embeddings
historical_watchlist.why: MoEMB scales universal multimodal embeddings along the expert axis and studies adaptive computation. With only 3B active parameters it surpasses reasoning-token embedding methods using over 4x active parameters, but the current abstract emphasizes active compute and quality rather than measured serving latency or throughput, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Dense Structural Compression of Transformers via Gauge-Correct Channel Removal
historical_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / dense structural compression / efficient inference
historical_watchlist.why: GaugeLasso learns structurally removable transformer channels while retaining dense tensors suitable for GPU execution, achieving very large FMA compression on controlled tasks and discovering depth-dependent compact architectures. The evidence is scientifically interesting but currently centered on synthetic/statistical tasks without measured LLM-serving latency, so retain as watch.

historical_watchlist.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge perception / human-robot interaction
historical_watchlist.why: SocioGesture uses a compact confidence-aware skeleton representation and lightweight dual-stream model for low-latency onboard social-gesture recognition, and runs in real time on a robot-mounted edge device with deployment-time adaptation. It is useful protected Physical-AI runtime evidence, but the abstract lacks concrete latency/throughput numbers.

historical_watchlist.title: BIO-MEMART: Biometric-Aware KV Cache Memory for Multi-User LLM Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning/agent systems / shared memory
historical_watchlist.why: Bio-MemArt adds biometric authorization to reusable KV-memory blocks while preserving MemArt latent retrieval and direct cache reuse. Its efficiency study reduces average prefill tokens from 18,781.96 full-context to 28.57, but the main novelty is access control rather than serving acceleration, so retain as a high-value KV/agent watch.

historical_watchlist.title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal MoE / reactive control
historical_watchlist.why: CR-VLA-Force explicitly targets the latency and action-chunk limitations of force-aware VLA control using a multimodal MoE plus VLA-guided adaptive compliance controller, and validates on real contact-rich tasks. It is accepted by IEEE RA-L and highly relevant to reactive Physical-AI deployment, but the current primary abstract does not provide measured end-to-end latency or throughput numbers, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: OpenWAM: An Open, Modular Exploration Towards Systematic World-Action Model Pretraining
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / WAM infrastructure / deployment stack
historical_watchlist.why: OpenWAM provides an open modular infrastructure that factorizes WAM model, representation, training, inference, deployment and evaluation choices, with released code, checkpoints, data recipes and real-robot evaluation across multiple embodiments. It is important infrastructure for the protected WAM direction, but the paper currently emphasizes modularity, scaling and task performance rather than measured serving speedup, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Streaming Hierarchical Inference with Tabular Foundation Models
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / hierarchical inference / selective offloading
historical_watchlist.why: HINT combines sliding-window graph ANN retrieval at the edge with uncertainty-aware selective offloading to a cloud-hosted tabular foundation model, explicitly trading predictive quality against communication and latency. It is a clean edge-cloud inference pattern, but the current abstract reports favorable trade-offs without concrete throughput/latency gains, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Building Pretraining Data for World Models: An Unreal Engine-Based Pipeline for Action-Conditioned Video Generation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world-model infrastructure / distributed data pipeline
historical_watchlist.why: This is a production-scale synthetic-data system for action-conditioned world models, with cache-aware partitioning, node-local slot scheduling, recovery, async upload and health monitoring across 25 servers with 8 RTX 5090 GPUs each, producing thousands of hours of video for EchoWM. The systems scale is valuable, but the abstract does not report comparative throughput or serving speedup, so retain as high-value infrastructure watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Real-Time dApps for AI-RAN: Measured Interface Requirements for Inline PHY and Slot-Level Control
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / AI-RAN / low-latency runtime interface
historical_watchlist.why: This work measures the interface requirements of AI-RAN dApps under live-cell load and shows that only in-process paths continue meeting 100-us control deadlines for bounded/inline workloads once the DU is active. It provides unusually concrete systems measurements and a released ABI, but is adjacent to the core ML-serving focus, so retain as high-value edge-infrastructure watch.

historical_watchlist.title: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world-model infrastructure / long-horizon inference
historical_watchlist.why: SolarWM provides a unified data/training/inference framework across Wan2.2, LTX-2.5 and MiniMax-H3 backbones and supports interactive rollouts from minutes to hours after training on 5-second sequences. It is highly relevant open world-model infrastructure, but the abstract does not provide comparative serving latency/throughput numbers, so retain as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: RoboDreamer: Anticipatory Humanoid Locomotion with Predictive State-Space Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / humanoid control / action chunking
historical_watchlist.why: RoboDreamer combines predictive state-space modeling, temporal masking/distillation and optional multi-step action chunking for robust humanoid locomotion, with real-time deployment on Unitree G1. The abstract indicates real-time latency but does not quantify serving speedup, so retain as a protected Physical-AI watch item.

historical_watchlist.title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / autonomous driving / non-autoregressive action
historical_watchlist.why: LaPla uses concurrent action queries in one forward pass and a frozen VQ-VAE decoder to bypass time-consuming autoregressive action generation. Closed-loop AlpaSim results report substantially reduced inference latency and strong success gains, but the abstract lacks a concrete latency/speedup number, so retain as protected Physical-AI watch.

historical_watchlist.title: FALCON-S: Fixed-wing ground-effect Aerodynamics Simulator and Flight Control Learning Suite
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / GPU simulation / robot learning
historical_watchlist.why: FALCON-S provides modular high-fidelity 6DoF fixed-wing ground-effect simulation with CPU and NVIDIA Warp GPU backends and high-throughput parallel execution for RL and optimal-control rollouts. It is valuable Physical-AI simulation infrastructure, but the abstract gives no comparative throughput figures.

historical_watchlist.title: Functional-SLAM: Interaction-Aware Mapping with Online Functional Scene Graphs
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / online mapping / scene graphs
historical_watchlist.why: Functional-SLAM maintains functional scene graphs online rather than relying on offline reconstruction, with substantially improved runtime while retaining competitive accuracy and enabling topology-assisted loop closure. The lack of concrete latency/throughput values keeps it as a high-value Physical-AI watch.

historical_watchlist.title: BLINK: Batch Normalization-based Integrity Checkpoints for In-Situ Detection and Mitigation of Diverse Weight Corruptions in DNN Accelerators
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / accelerator reliability / runtime
historical_watchlist.why: BLINK performs autonomous on-chip inference-time corruption detection and mitigation without host intervention or fine-tuning data, with >99% detection precision and under 2% latency overhead. It is valuable accelerator-runtime resilience work but not primarily an efficiency contribution, so retain as watch.

historical_watchlist.title: LightSplat: Real-Time High-Fidelity 3D Gaussian SLAM with Loop Closure
historical_watchlist.why: LightSplat combines sparse tracking with a dual-thread dense Gaussian backend and online loop closure, sustaining about 8 FPS on real-world robotic deployment while preserving reconstruction quality. It is directly relevant real-time 3DGS robotics infrastructure, but stronger comparative speedup evidence is still missing.

historical_watchlist.title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent memory / retrieval / LLM-free memory management
historical_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a directly relevant efficient-agent memory paper absent from authority. EdgeMem preserves original turns and constructs/retrieves memory through lightweight local multi-anchor hypergraph processing, requiring no generative-LLM calls for memory construction or retrieval. Retained as high-value watch because the current abstract demonstrates quality and removal of generative memory calls but does not report hard end-to-end latency/throughput speedup.

historical_watchlist.title: Do Dynamic Routers Need Memory? HeRo: History-Aware Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
historical_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / dynamic layer routing / efficient LLM inference / router memory
historical_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a relevant dynamic-routing paper absent from authority. HeRo conditions token-wise FFN routing on an explicit history state built with linear attention; on Llama 3.1-8B it reports 100.24% dense-model aggregate performance while bypassing 26.87% of parameters, and 97.01% performance while bypassing 38.82%. Retained as high-value watch because the abstract does not report measured wall-clock latency or throughput gains.

historical_watchlist.title: Jacap: Robust KV Cache Eviction via Jacobian-Based Nonlinear Information Capacity Preservation
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / eviction / information geometry / cache compression
historical_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a theoretically grounded KV-cache eviction method absent from authority. Jacap derives a Jacobian information-capacity objective for nonlinear softmax attention and uses softmax-aware importance plus statistical leverage scores for cache subset selection, with strongest gains reported in high-compression regimes. Retained as high-value watch because the current evidence is quality-under-compression rather than measured serving latency/throughput.

historical_watchlist.title: Scaling Bimanual Household Manipulation from 1,500 hours of Demonstrations to On-Policy Corrections
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / bimanual manipulation / data pipeline / training efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: 7d protected Physical-AI replay recovered XR-2 and its 1,500-hour bimanual demonstration corpus. The work explicitly uses a purpose-built high-throughput data pipeline and multi-stage training paradigm and reports favorable training efficiency/data utilization, but the current abstract lacks comparative throughput/latency or systems-speedup numbers, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

historical_watchlist.title: NSFlow: End-to-End Differentiable Neuro-Symbolic Optical Flow for Visual Odometry
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embedded visual odometry / realtime perception / efficient robotics
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a hybrid CNN plus differentiable Lucas-Kanade optical-flow front-end that is explicitly designed for efficient VO/VIO and reports realtime embedded deployment with lower latency than purely regression-based alternatives. The abstract does not expose a directly comparable absolute latency or speedup figure, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Sensing Which Modality Matters: Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust VLA Policies
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal robustness / zero-overhead inference / sensor fusion
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a VLA robustness method whose evidence-gated regularization adds zero inference-time overhead and substantially improves real-robot robustness under sensor corruption and distractors. Because the core contribution is algorithmic robustness rather than measured serving acceleration or systems throughput, it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: FWBC-VLA: Force-Aware Whole-Body Compensation for Contact-Rich Loco-Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / contact-rich manipulation / action decoding / whole-body control
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a VLA-to-whole-body-control bridge that estimates contact without force sensors and injects contact-state tokens during action decoding, then generates corrective whole-body actions for real robot loco-manipulation. Real-world wiping and door-opening experiments demonstrate deployment relevance, but the current abstract does not provide comparative serving latency, throughput, memory, or compute-speedup numbers, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Tools-CC-Bench: a Benchmark Suite for Collective Communication with Compression in HPC and AI Workloads
historical_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / collective communication / compression / systems benchmarking
historical_watchlist.why: 7d replay recovered an application-oriented benchmark for compression-enabled collectives across realistic HPC and LLM workloads. CC-Bench profiles per-phase latency, hardware utilization, fidelity and computation interference across CPU/GPU clusters and multiple communication libraries. It is highly relevant infrastructure for communication-compression evaluation, but the abstract primarily contributes methodology and characterization rather than a new universally faster runtime, so it is retained as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: The OCUDU dApp Platform: An Open Runtime and E3 Interface for Real-Time AI-RAN
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / real-time AI-RAN / GPU runtime / edge orchestration
historical_watchlist.why: Protected edge/heterogeneous replay recovered an open production-DU runtime that supports GPU-resident receive-chain apps, scheduler-path apps under a 100 us admitted deadline, and never-blocking observer apps. Live GB10 gNB validation shows all three classes running together without fallback. It is highly relevant real-time AI infrastructure, but the abstract does not provide a comparative throughput or speedup baseline, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Anti-Gravity Walking by a Flying Humanoid Robot via Thrust-Rate Input Whole-Body Model Predictive Control
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot control / real-time MPC / humanoid
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a real-time whole-body MPC implementation for a flying humanoid, including sparse optimal-control structure and hardware demonstration under contact switching. This is deployment-relevant compute/control evidence, but the abstract does not provide absolute controller latency, throughput, or a comparative runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Bringing dApps to OCUDU: An E3 Controller for Real-Time Open RAN Intelligence
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / real-time AI-RAN / Open RAN / runtime interfaces
historical_watchlist.why: 7d protected edge replay recovered an open-source E3Controller for OCUDU that enables sub-millisecond dApp access/control through a sidecar design and validates real-time I/Q delivery on a production-grade Open RAN stack with no measurable throughput penalty. It is valuable runtime/interface infrastructure, but lacks a comparative speedup or broader AI workload efficiency result, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / dexterous manipulation / tactile fusion / world modeling
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI candidate. DeCAL combines specialized MoT experts, adaptive visuo-tactile fusion, and latent co-imagination for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, reaching 71% average success and 83.4% progress success. The current primary abstract does not report serving latency, throughput, memory, or a comparative runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

historical_watchlist.title: Ozaki 2.5: Engineering the Deconstruction Path of fp64-Emulated Dense Matrix Multiplication on FP8 Tensor Cores
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / FP8 tensor cores / mixed precision / GEMM / architecture co-design
historical_watchlist.why: High-value mixed-precision architecture/kernel work on FP64-emulated GEMM over FP8 tensor cores, including residue conversion, pipelining and a proposed stream-side conversion mechanism. The paper explicitly states that every performance result is a model projection pending measurement, so projected 235-473 TFLOPS and 1.6-1.9x gains are not promoted as measured systems evidence.

historical_watchlist.title: Omni Interaction Agent Technical Report
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / efficient reasoning/agent systems / streaming full-duplex runtime
historical_watchlist.why: Gander is directly relevant to realtime multimodal agent infrastructure: a Cerebellum-Brain split, streaming Thinker-Talker, chunk-level ordered token stream, tool calling and an agent orchestration runtime support continuous full-duplex video/speech/text interaction and interruption. The primary report does not give hard end-to-end latency/throughput numbers for the orchestration design, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: GraphFAS: A Distributed System for Automated Graph Feature Generation and Selection in Industrial Transaction Networks
historical_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / industrial graph systems / feature pipeline / production deployment
historical_watchlist.why: Production distributed graph-feature system deployed at Alipay, with explicit graph feature generation and distributed Boruta-style selection and reported order-of-magnitude engineering-efficiency improvement. This is useful production infrastructure evidence, but the abstract lacks a concrete throughput/latency/speedup baseline, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: SkillAdam: Stable and Efficient Skill Evolution for Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / skill optimization / agent memory / cost reduction
historical_watchlist.why: Relevant efficient-agent work: optimization memory stabilizes discrete skill updates and a volatility-driven edit budget adapts revision scope; across seven benchmarks it reports stronger skills with substantially fewer optimization iterations and lower cost than prior methods. Because the primary abstract gives no concrete wall-clock/token/cost reduction numbers, it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: It's Not RoPE that Creates Sinks: The Role of Self-Concentration and Value-Non-Mixing in Attention
historical_watchlist.topic: quantization / attention / massive activations / low-bit robustness
historical_watchlist.why: Mechanistic analysis directly relevant to low-bit quantization: it attributes attention sinks and massive activations to causal-mask-induced self-concentration and value non-mixing rather than RoPE. It may inform future quantization strategies, but it proposes no quantizer and reports no measured inference efficiency benefit, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: ECOKV: Geometry-Aware KV Cache Eviction via Complementary Diversity Metrics
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / multimodal MLLM serving / cache eviction
historical_watchlist.why: Directly relevant KV-cache compression work for multimodal LLMs: complementary Euclidean and cosine diversity metrics estimate per-head redundancy and adaptively balance diversity and importance while reducing the recent-token observation window. The primary abstract reports state-of-the-art quality across compression ratios but no measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or memory-speedup number, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: RoboSPA: Can VLA Models Go Beyond Simple Scenes and Short-Horizon Tasks?
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / benchmark / long-horizon embodied reasoning
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark with 10 task categories, 56 base tasks, 280 difficulty variants and 527K trajectories across multiple embodiments. It exposes spatial, execution, and memory-intensive planning failures in current VLAs and provides official data/code, but it is primarily a diagnostic benchmark rather than an efficiency/runtime contribution, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: KBBQ: A Predictive Noise Law and the Limits of Spectrum Flattening in FP4 Quantization
historical_watchlist.why: High-value FP4 quantization work with a closed-form second-order noise law and Kappa-Braked Blockwise Quantization. Across four base models and two FP4 formats, KBBQ improves W4A4 quality over prior state of the art without additional deployment-time computation. The primary abstract does not report measured latency/throughput or memory speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: MobileVLA-R1 2.0: RL-Enhanced Reasoning for Mobile Robot Control
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / mobile robot control / reasoning-action decoupling
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work coupling structured embodied reasoning with a reasoning-conditioned action decoder and embodiment-specific controllers, evaluated on navigation, quadruped control and real Unitree Go2/G1 deployments. It improves task success but reports no serving/runtime efficiency metric, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: WorldAgen: Unified State-Action Prediction with Test-Time World Model Training
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / test-time adaptation
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work unifying world-state prediction and action prediction with lightweight test-time training to adapt world dynamics in unseen environments. It improves CALVIN/LIBERO performance after a small number of test-time samples, but the primary abstract gives no measured test-time overhead, latency or throughput, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Accelerating Atom Simulations with Variable-Block Sparse Matrix Library
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / distributed sparse linear algebra / scientific AI infrastructure
historical_watchlist.why: VBCSR preserves variable-size atomic blocks and groups equal-shape blocks for optimized dense-kernel dispatch, with a unified CSR/BSR/VBCSR interface and a demonstration above one million atoms. The abstract states it outperforms tested Python-accessible references but does not expose a quantified end-to-end speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving / multi-tenant security characterization
historical_watchlist.why: Seven experiments on live shared LLM serving show that KV-cache timing side-channel reliability collapses under realistic contention; on a two-node two-GPU tensor-parallel vLLM setup mean effect size drops from 3.418 to 0.511. This is valuable multi-tenant KV-cache systems characterization rather than an efficiency-improving runtime, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Interactive Debugger for Performance Portable Python HPC Kernels
historical_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / Python HPC / developer tooling
historical_watchlist.why: PKDB adds breakpoints, stepping, inspection, live code evaluation and hot kernel substitution while preserving on-device PyKokkos execution across CPU/GPU backends. The primary abstract reports limited overhead but no quantified workload speedup; it is retained as high-value runtime/tooling infrastructure.

historical_watchlist.title: ICI-VLA: In-Context Imitation with Spatiotemporally Aligned Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / test-time adaptation / retrieval-conditioned control
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work keeps the VLA fixed at inference and adapts through retrieved phase- and geometry-aligned micro-demonstrations, reaching 97.7% LIBERO, 60.4% RoboTwin 2.0 and 83.2% across four physical tasks. No measured serving latency/throughput benefit is reported, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: GIFT: Goal-Injected Fine-Tuning for Efficient Manipulation Policy Adaptation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / lightweight adaptation / goal-conditioned manipulation
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work injects generated goal-image features into pretrained VLA policies through zero-initialized convolution; one epoch of fine-tuning improves reported task success by 4.7-13.4 percentage points. The efficiency claim is adaptation-oriented and the abstract lacks serving/runtime measurements, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: PACO: A Fully Cache-Oblivious Parallel FFT with One Global Redistribution
historical_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / parallel FFT / communication-efficient HPC
historical_watchlist.why: PACO fuses deferred cache-oblivious layout changes into the single redistribution already required by the parallel FFT, proving optimal local cache complexity and exactly one global redistribution round under its ownership model. The current paper is primarily theoretical and exposes no measured end-to-end hardware speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / long-context / constant-memory recurrent inference
historical_watchlist.why: KDN reformulates recurrent associative memory as a linear-Gaussian state-space model and introduces scan-compatible diagonal and isotropic approximations whose uncertainty recurrences admit associative scans with logarithmic parallel depth. It improves perplexity and downstream accuracy over strong linear-attention baselines, but the abstract does not report measured latency/throughput gains, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot memory / benchmark
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark separates robot-memory Storage, Update and Compression across 30 history-dependent tasks, 1,500 demonstrations and 4,200 executable checkpoints; the strongest memory baseline reaches only 31.9% average success. It is important diagnostic infrastructure but not an efficiency-improving runtime, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: RoboTok: An Internet-Scale Data Engine for Human Demonstration Retrieval and Dexterous Manipulation Learning
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / data engine / scalable demonstration retrieval
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work builds an internet-scale motion-retrieval data engine using compact actor-centered 3D hand-trajectory embeddings for efficient search and continual indexing, and improves downstream dexterous manipulation policy success. The available primary description does not quantify retrieval latency/throughput or systems speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond Retrieval: Progressive Latent Memory Evolution for Streaming Video Understanding
historical_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / bounded latent memory
historical_watchlist.why: LatentStream targets continuous causal video understanding under a fixed memory budget, using hierarchical streaming memory and compact fixed-length evolving latent tokens. It reports SOTA quality but no measured latency/throughput/system speedup in the primary abstract, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Performance Study of Serverless Workloads in Confidential Virtual Machines
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / confidential serverless / memory and startup overhead
historical_watchlist.why: This empirical systems study characterizes warm/cold-start and memory-efficiency overheads of serverless workloads inside confidential VMs, identifying page-deduplication/reclaimability and VMEXIT effects and practical mitigation directions. It is high-value cloud-systems characterization, but not a new broadly faster runtime with headline speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Hyperparameter Scaling Laws Across MoE Sparsity
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / sparse training / scaling laws
historical_watchlist.why: The work runs 1,800 pre-training experiments spanning six activated-parameter scales, about 20T tokens and 200k H800-equivalent GPU-hours, deriving scaling laws that explicitly include activation ratio and validating on a 12B ultra-sparse MoE with 1/64 experts active. It is important MoE efficiency methodology but does not introduce a measured systems/runtime speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Quantization Amplifies Determinism, Not Bias: Scale-Dependent Behavioral Effects of Serving-Time Weight Compression
historical_watchlist.why: This controlled serving-time study compares Qwen3 8B/14B/32B under W4A16 AWQ, W8A16 FP8-Marlin and BF16 across about 71k paired completions, finding scale-dependent output concentration and stylistic drift. It is valuable deployment-quality evidence for quantization, but it does not claim a new quantization runtime or measured speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Beyond Retraining-Free MoE Compression: A Cost-Normalized Study of Post-Compression Adjustment
historical_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / compression / deployment memory / adjustment cost
historical_watchlist.why: This study evaluates four MoE pruning/merging methods on two MoE LLM backbones with matched GPU-cost accounting and shows that a tiny one-epoch post-compression adjustment on 3,000 C4 examples recovers 37.3% of the original-to-compressed performance gap on average. It is useful deployment-efficiency evidence, but it does not provide a new serving runtime or measured latency/throughput speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Separating Stream Stability from Long-Term Recall in Language Models
historical_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / streaming LLM / constant-memory evaluation
historical_watchlist.why: ThreeH separates stability, access and utility horizons under a common state/compute budget and shows that attention-sink streaming can remain stable indefinitely while losing semantic access outside the active cache. It is an important systems-evaluation contract for constant-memory streaming and cache/recurrent/retrieval designs, but it does not introduce a new measured faster runtime, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Distributed Dexterous Manipulation with Spatially Conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multi-agent transformer / dexterous manipulation
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work uses spatially conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers for an 8x8 array of 64 soft delta robots and introduces action selection that maintains real-world manipulation accuracy around 1.5 cm while using about 65% fewer robots. This is meaningful resource-use evidence, but the primary abstract does not report inference latency/throughput or compute speedup, so it remains watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: Nyström Attention Matches Full Attention for Cross-Sectional Stock Prediction
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / low-rank attention / linear-complexity approximation
historical_watchlist.why: This controlled attention decomposition finds the learned cross-sectional attention deviation to be low-rank and shows Nystrom attention with 32 landmarks matches full O(N^2) attention at O(mN) cost, with statistical equivalence at N=300 and N=800. It is useful evidence for low-rank rather than sparse attention structure, but the primary abstract does not report measured latency, throughput, memory or energy gains, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: MomentQuant: an even more minimalist interval method with linear time complexity for time series classification
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient inference / linear-time algorithms
historical_watchlist.why: MomentQuant replaces exact interval quantiles with Cornish-Fisher approximations, removes the sorting requirement and reduces inference complexity to linear time. The primary abstract reports the optimized Quant implementation is faster than the original and MomentQuant is faster again with only a tiny predictive-performance decrease, making it relevant to lightweight inference; however, no numeric deployment latency/throughput gain is given in the primary abstract, so it remains watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: TriCCOT: Tri-part Convolutional Conformal Transformer for Onboard Space Object Detection
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / FPGA / efficient attention
historical_watchlist.why: TriCCOT replaces FPGA-unfriendly Transformer operations with convolutional projections, global channel statistics and hardware-friendly gating, and reports full unified CNN-Transformer deployment on a Xilinx Versal VCK190 without DPU modification. This is strong deployability evidence, but the primary abstract does not give measured latency, throughput, memory or energy gains, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: FailureSpot: Label-Efficient Timestamp-Level Failure Detection for Vision-Language-Action Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / failure detection / runtime safety
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work derives weak supervision directly from VLA action chunks and uses active learning for sparse timestamp annotations, improving both timestamp-level and trajectory-level failure detection across multiple VLA policies. It targets deployment reliability with lightweight proactive detection but reports no direct runtime latency/throughput gain in the primary abstract, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: VLA-Corrector: Stage-Aware Observable State Understanding for Prompt-Based Closed-Loop Recovery of Vision-Language-Action Policies
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / closed-loop recovery / runtime verifier
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work adds an observable-history Learned Verifier over multi-view vision, proprioception and executed actions, then produces stage-conditioned recovery prompts for the same frozen VLA policy without privileged simulator state. LIBERO and LIBERO Plus evaluations show substantially improved closed-loop reliability, but no measured serving overhead or throughput is reported in the primary abstract, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: From Splats to Silicon: Rethinking Computational Efficiency of 3DGS
historical_watchlist.why: This workload-centric 3DGS systems study connects representation changes, GPU runtime optimization and hardware architecture, with reproduced measurements and controlled GPU profiling that trace workload counts into stage time and memory traffic. It is highly relevant to efficient-3DGS systems methodology, but its contribution is synthesis and characterization rather than a single new faster runtime, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Predictive Zonotope Reduction: Precise Runtime Monitoring under Uncertainty
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / runtime monitoring / edge safety
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work dynamically selects zonotope reduction via beam-search MPC and distills the policy into a small neural policy for substantially faster execution while maintaining improved monitoring precision. Implemented in RLola and evaluated on Raspberry Pi 5 for a robotic-arm workload. The primary abstract lacks an exact latency/speedup number, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

historical_watchlist.title: HiSfM: Disambiguating Structure-from-Motion via Scaffold-Anchored Hierarchical Reconstruction
historical_watchlist.why: Hierarchical coarse-to-fine SfM builds a compact verified scaffold and then absorbs remaining images, improving robustness under repeated/symmetric structure while substantially reducing runtime versus prior methods. Official author code is available, but the primary abstract does not report an exact latency or speedup figure, so it is retained as high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: PPO-STGNN: A Proximal Policy Optimization Approach with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for DAG Task Scheduling in Cloud-Edge-End Computing
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / scheduling / reinforcement learning
historical_watchlist.why: DAG scheduling across heterogeneous cloud-edge-end resources using STGNN state encoding plus PPO and multi-teacher behavior-cloning pretraining. Experiments report better load balancing while maintaining low completion time, but the primary abstract provides no exact latency/makespan gain, so this remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent memory / context management
historical_watchlist.why: Task-conditioned memory clearance uses LOO screening plus sampled cooperative Shapley attribution to suppress harmful memories without modifying the persistent store. Across ten long-dialogue memory pools it reaches 85.9% target recall and 82.3% task recovery, +25.5 points over LOO, but no direct token/latency reduction is reported, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: R2S-Eval: Robot Evaluation with Real-to-Sim Calibration via Vision-Language Models
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / evaluation infrastructure / real-to-sim
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI evaluation infrastructure calibrates simulation to a real setup and uses VLM preference judgments to reduce repeated hardware trials and operator effort while producing stable policy rankings. Real and simulated experiments support the workflow, but the abstract gives no exact evaluation-time or hardware-effort reduction, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: CoordFormer: Give Me Any Coordinates and I Will Give You Labels
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / high-resolution inference / edge-cloud vision
historical_watchlist.why: Coordinate decoding with localized cross-attention combines downsampled global ViT tokens and high-resolution local patches, supporting semantic-edge-focused inference that reduces memory, latency and compute on very-high-resolution segmentation. SOTA accuracy is reported, but the abstract omits exact speedup/memory numbers, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Resilience Beyond Stationary Client Unavailability: Unlocking Efficient and Unbiased Federated Learning
historical_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / federated learning / dynamic availability
historical_watchlist.why: FedSWE targets heterogeneous non-stationary client availability with missed-computation compensation, stabilized global updates and implicit gossip mixing while remaining agnostic to the availability process. It adds only light memory/compute overhead and has linear-speedup theory in special cases, but the primary abstract gives no exact measured runtime/communication reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: SimSkill: A Lifelong Learning AI Agent for Autonomous Mastery of Traffic Simulation
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent memory / reusable skills
historical_watchlist.why: Self-evolving SUMO agent identifies capability gaps, generates and verifies environment-grounded tasks, and consolidates episodic/procedural/semantic memory without backbone updates. It improves verified completion by up to 25 percentage points, but memory benefits are model- and budget-dependent and do not uniformly reduce inference cost, so it remains watch. Official code/data repository is author-provided.

historical_watchlist.title: Sparse auto-regressive modeling for scene generation from multi-view images
historical_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / sparse 3D generation / 3D Gaussian Splatting
historical_watchlist.why: SPAR3S learns a compact voxel-aligned 3D latent space in which only occupied voxels are represented, then jointly predicts sparse occupancy and latent tokens with a masked autoregressive transformer. The sparse representation directly targets dense-volumetric compute cost and uses differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting supervision, but the primary abstract reports no exact runtime or memory reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: HaptiNet: Networked Haptic Robots Enable Physical Co-presence in Geographically-Unconstrained Rehabilitation
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / distributed robotics / network delay compensation
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI infrastructure: networked haptic robots use an imitation-learning delay compensator to preserve force-mediated interaction over geographically distributed links. Validation spans 284 healthy participants, 111 patients, and three intercity links totaling about 4,000 km. The work demonstrates robust distributed physical interaction but does not report a compute/serving speedup, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / RAG / soft context compression / inference efficiency
historical_watchlist.why: DEX-Comp directly targets the inference overhead of long retrieved contexts by encoding documents into substantially shorter embedding sequences. Its two-stage recipe first distills correct uncompressed-RAG behavior, then uses RL only on cases the uncompressed system fails. This is highly relevant to serving efficiency, but the primary abstract emphasizes QA quality across retrieval depths and does not provide a measured latency/throughput or token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Query-Oblivious Coresets for Softmax Attention: Improved Bounds and Efficient Constructions
historical_watchlist.why: Constructs query-oblivious subsets of key-value pairs that approximate softmax attention uniformly over a query ball, improving coreset-size bounds and giving randomized polynomial-time constructions. This is directly relevant to principled attention compression, but current evidence is theoretical rather than measured accelerator/runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: OctWorld: Long-Range World-Consistent Video Generation with Octree-Based 3D Mapping
historical_watchlist.topic: video/image generation acceleration / world models / sparse 3D memory
historical_watchlist.why: OctWorld adds a persistent OctMap memory using TSDF fusion in a dynamic sparse octree to stabilize long-range autoregressive video world generation under revisits. The sparse adaptive 3D memory is structurally relevant to efficient world-model generation, but the primary abstract does not report a concrete latency, throughput, or memory reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Real-Time Shape Control of Multi-Segment Soft Robotic Arms Using Koopman Operators with Global and Local Observables
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-time robot control / model-based runtime
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work: a Koopman-MPC controller combines global and local observables for real-time full-shape control, scales numerically to 10 independently actuated segments, and is physically validated on 3- and 5-segment arms at tip speeds up to 0.6 m/s, with robustness to 400 g payloads and 7 N disturbances. It is a strong real-time control result, but not a serving/computation speedup paper, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Efficiency Methods for Multi-Agent Systems
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent efficiency / evaluation methodology
historical_watchlist.why: Directly audits claimed efficiency gains in LLM multi-agent systems under a shared backbone, agent registry, runtime, topology, scale, depth, and tool-use controls. It shows that apparent gains can come from structural collapse, disabled tool pathways, or weak starting systems where random pruning already preserves accuracy. This is important for evaluating agent-efficiency papers, but it is primarily a diagnostic benchmark rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: LoGIC: Budgeted Context Construction for Node-Level Graph In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models
historical_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / efficient attention / context budgeting / graph in-context learning
historical_watchlist.why: LoGIC targets the quadratic attention, preprocessing, and memory bottlenecks caused by using the full labeled training table as graph-ICL context. It allocates labeled-context and unlabeled-halo budgets, shares context within graph-local query clusters, and reports markedly lower peak memory while preserving locally runnable full-context performance and enabling frozen graph ICL on million-node graphs. The primary abstract lacks an exact latency or memory-reduction factor, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hierarchical agent runtime / decentralized robot control
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work that cleanly separates expensive LLM reasoning from fast local control: LLM inference is confined to round-level policy generation/refinement while a UCB bandit and policy-conditioned Double DQN execute tick-level actions. In the evaluated three-robot simulation, the complete configuration reached all 90 robot-round goals and achieved 42-tick median completion time, 25.0-39.1% lower than alternative configurations. The evidence is simulation-level task efficiency rather than measured inference latency/throughput, so it remains watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Diagnosing and Dynamically Filtering Occupancy World Models for Active Mapping
historical_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world-model runtime / active mapping / occupancy filtering
historical_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI/world-model work that isolates how occupancy completion errors alter both exploration choices and motion feasibility, then studies dynamic filtering of learned occupancy for active mapping. The planner is held fixed so the effect of the world-model representation is attributable, making this useful for world-model runtime reliability and selective-use policies. It does not present a direct serving or compute speedup metric in the primary abstract, so it remains high-value watch.

historical_watchlist.title: Inference-Time Graph Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
historical_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent orchestration / inference-time workflow graphs
historical_watchlist.why: ReActNet compiles each query into task-conditioned temporal communication graphs with edge-level message semantics, separating graph compilation from execution without RL or gradient-based topology optimization.
